utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Today Judge Kinis is unable to sit. Judge Gwaunza and myself have decided that we're satisfied that it's in the interests of justice to continue today to hear the case. We expect Judge Kinis to be back on Monday. Mr. Mikulicic, are you ready to continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Janic, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Please proceed, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Janic. You may remember we discussed yesterday the order of the then-chief of Main Staff, General Bobetko, instructing special police units to assemble on Mount Velebit. Later on, this order was withdrawn. You understood this to be a kind of exercise for the forthcoming operation. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see document 65 ter 00683.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to be shown, this is an order of the new order of General Zvonimir Cervenko dated 21 of June, 1995, in which he says that elements of the special police of the MUP of Croatia be dispatched to Zadar, Vir, and Nin areas by 2000 hours on the 23rd of July, and the number of men should be 300. Mr. Janic, do you remember if this order was complied with, the order issued by General Cervenko?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I earlier spoke about what we did in the area of Zadar. This was the reserve of special police for a potential intervention on the line of defence near the town of Zadar. That was at the time immediately before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number D537.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D537 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have 65 ter 01818.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The following day, that is, the 22nd of July, the Main Staff of the Croatian army. It's signed here on behalf of the chief by General Stipecic. Another order was issued to the district area Split and the command post in Zadar, saying that accommodation needs to be provided for 350 members of the special police. If you look at item 4, it says: "The special police forces will be under direct command of the Main Staff of the Croatian army." So this is a follow-up or a continuation of the developments on the eve of Operation Storm. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This order gives more details than the previous one, but they are related.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have the number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D538, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D538 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now see the document already tendered into evidence by the Prosecution, and the number is P554.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This document is dated the 22nd of July, 1995. It actually set up the staff of joint special police forces. The order signed - but you will see this on the next page - by Mr. Jarnjak, minister of the interior, and the assistant minister, Mr. Markac, is based on the order of the -- order of General Zvonimir Cervenko; and it refers to the engagement of joint special police forces equalling the strength of a battalion in the area of Zadar and Knin. Further on, the order stipulates that as at 23rd July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading this from the first page of this order. Perhaps we can move down the English version. The Croatian version is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So the order is given that: "On 23rd of July, the staff of special police joint forces is going to start operating with a command post in the Zadar-Knin police administration, and appointed to the staff the following officers of the Ministry of Interior are appointed: "Action commander, assistant minister Colonel-General Mladen Markac; Chief of Staff, Brigadier Zeljko Sacic; head of the internal control department; Major Ante Soljic; assistant for intervention squad Colonel Svemir Vrsaljko. Let us stop here. Tell us more about this action code-name "Poskok 2"?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned this operation yesterday. It was an action launched in the area of Velebit with the aim of providing protection of the highway linking the northern and southern parts of Croatia, the Adriatic Highway. It was in place from 1992 up until Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 5 says that based on this order, Major Zdravko Janic was appointed to the staff. That's you, right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Other persons are mentioned here, such as assistant for infantry; under item number 9, we have assistant for intelligence and operations, Damir Cvetko; assistant for rocket and artillery support, Captain Anton Basic; assistant for logistics, Stjepan Kocmanic; assistant for communications, Drago Kelebuh; assistant for medical support, Dr. Josip Mihailovic; coordinator for the Croatian army, Captain Mladen Puceh; and assistant for reserve force, Slavo Maduna. So we see that appointed to the staff were 15 persons all together. Further on, it says that the staff is -- shall, on the 23rd of July, no later than 1600 hours -- The next part of this order says that the command of the joint forces is to perform their task in a professional manner in accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs and the conventions of the international law of war. It also says that during the carrying out of missions, the command shall keep a war log and draw up maps; and upon the completion of the task, it is should analyse operations and submit a original report. Mr. Janic, in order for to us make these military terms more understandable as civilians, tell us, what was the main purpose of the staff of joint forces?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special police joint forces staff was within an operation carried out together with the Croatian army is to carry out tasks assigned to the special police and in the area assigned to the special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Speaking of the area of responsibility, were the special police in actions of these type had responsibility over a specific territory in terms of creating preconditions for the subsequent functioning of civilian authorities; or was the territorial jurisdiction of special police absent, or rather, you had just an area of responsibility. Can you explain that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any operation in which the special police took part, only -- it only had an area of responsibility for this specific task from the beginning until the end of it. For example, in Operation Storm, it was far -- four or five days. The special police had no territorial jurisdiction in any area whatsoever. So we are talking exclusively about an area of responsibility for the duration of a specific operation. As soon as the objectives of the action were achieved, the special police was removed from the area and did not carry out any official tasks. After that, regular police would take over the territorial jurisdiction in a certain area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So one might say that actually the area of responsibility was the axis of operation of special police in a specific area?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. That was an axis of operation, in terms of a militarily planned action drawn up and carried out by the Main Staff. Along the front line, we would be assigned a certain sector and a certain area of responsibility, and that was our axis of operation. Once our mission was completed, we left the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I understand. Maybe you can give us some more explanation. Unlike special police, Croatian army units - and by that, I mean the military directs of Split and Gospic with whom you cooperated in Operation Storm - resolved this issue in a different way. They had a certain territorial jurisdiction. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please clarify your question. I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Sorry for putting it in such a complicated way. So, you explained to us what an area of responsibility of special police is. This Operation Storm took place in cooperation of two Military Districts. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Those are the Military Districts of Split, which was, as it were, your neighbour on the right flank?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And Military District Gospic, which was your neighbour to the left in the operation?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Those two Military Districts, Split and Gospic, were differently structured in terms of the area in relation to the special police. Could you tell us a little bit more about that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could. The entire territory of Croatia was divided into Military Districts. I don't know exactly how many of them there were, but each Military District would include an area that had territorial jurisdiction, such as, for instance, the police administrations of certain municipalities had jurisdiction over that area; whereas, the military had the jurisdiction over a wider area of several counties. In other words, there may have been four to five Military Districts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: All right. We will return to this subject a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For now, could I please -- could the witness please be shown document 65 ter 01819.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After a command was issued, an order was issued from the military staff and co-signed by Mr. Jarnjak and Mladen Markac. On the 22nd of July, 1995, Mr. Markac issued the order that can you see in front of you on the screen, which was addressed to the chief of Brod Posovina police. In the order, it is requested that on the 22nd of July, at 1800 hours --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the document, as I read it, is not addressed to the -- it says: "Attention, chief of Brod Posavina police administration," to be handed over to the specialised police unit commander. So to read it as an order addressed to the chief of the police administration is incorrect. The way I say it, he is being asked to hand it over to the special police unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it is not incorrect what Mr. Mikulicic says, although incomplete, because it is addressed to the Brod Posavina police administration, and what I understand is that a special police unit is one of the units or part of that. So it is incomplete, but not incorrect. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, in this order, the special police unit within the police administration of Brod Posavina is asked to assign certain members of the special police, including some equipment, including a mortar, a 120-millimetre battery, as well as a 128-millimetre laser guided missile launcher, to head directly toward the Zadar-Knin police administration in order to carry out tasks within the scope of work of the joint forces of the special police. Mr. Janic, do I read this correctly, that this is an order where the entire forces of the special police are being strengthened in manpower in this area, in Zadar below the Velebit mountain?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These orders actually ensured that special police members would come to certain areas; and, here, it refers to the special police that had already been in the area of Zadar, so that when the special police received this mortar, actually, its forces were strengthened and it was capable of defending the defence line on its own.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please assign a number to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number, D539, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D539 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar please pull up 65 ter 01817.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I meanwhile ask a question to the witness in relation to the last document. This document mentions a laser guided missile launcher. Could you tell us something about the position of -- you're nodding no. But including mortar -- could we have the previous document back for a second. You see that the orders says: "On the 22nd of July at 6.00 p.m., you shall take 120 members of your unit, including mortar 120-millimetre battery, as well as one 128-millimetre VRL laser guided missile launcher." Do you see that? Are you familiar with this laser guided missiles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am. This is a multiple rocket launcher, I think it had 12 barrels, and it could fire 12 rockets at the same time, 12 shells. It is a standard artillery weapon, short range. It is not a long range weapon, and its range is somewhat larger than the 120-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means -- yes. Now the fact that it was laser guided, would that have any impact on the position of targeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Maybe if the witness will take off his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take off your earphones for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe it is another translation mistake, because the abbreviation "VRL" in Croatian means multiple rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that's the case, then, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... there is no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I was caught by the word "laser guided."

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So we could ask the witness on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know, of course, how my words were translated to him. Could you tell us what "VRL" stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a multiple rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If that's all, then it appears that I'm always the unlucky one who catches the translation errors. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But I appreciate that, Your Honour, because I didn't see it, and it's of vital importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, position and targeting and laser guided might be different from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have the number. Could we now pull up document -- that's fine. This is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, the 22nd of July, an order, assistant minister Mladen Markac, sent to the attention of the chief of the Bjelovar-Bilogorska PU, with a note that it should be handed over to the commander of the special police forces in that police administration. We can see here almost an identical document where they're asking a 120 officers, including a mortar battery as well as a multiple rocket launcher should be sent to the area, so that they could within the scope of work of the joint forces operate in the area. Could you tell us, is this one of the way in which the joint forces were formed?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. Each unit that took part, whether in this case or in any other case, would receive this type of order for its use, for its employment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the translation on the -- on the screen is not that of the B/C/S version, because I see the B/C/S version is addressed to Bjelovar-Bilogorska; whereas, the translation is to chief of Brod Posavina. So I think the translation is from the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And it's the very same issue as it regards to VRL.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that. These are, you said, documents uploaded by the Prosecution, 65 ter documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: These are all 65 ter documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, you have got a little job to do, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: We have already asked for revised translations for all the documents, so it takes a while for the revised translations to be uploaded. Hopefully, it will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you look on the right side, there is -- under "number," it is 608/95 on the B/C/S version; and on the left in the English version, it is 607/95. So there are -- they are not the same document. In Croatian, it says "Broj," and then has 511-01-30-608/95. On the English version, it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can imagine that they have been mixed up because it seems that orders are passed in past to various addressees with almost similar language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that if you asked the translation to be revised, Ms. Mahindaratne, you will certainly insist in ensuring that we're talking about the same document, yes? Please proceed --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt again. If you see, the ERN numbers are the same on the left. The last four numbers are on 1264 on the top, and the last for numbers are 1264 on the B/C/S document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which would suggest that there they are still the same documents as far as ERN documents are concerned. But from the text, it appears that the translation is related to another, although perhaps a very similar document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least you've got something to do during the break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. Could I have a number for this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, for which one? The one or the other?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: For both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we wait until after the break until you have sorted this out; and then with right 65 ter numbers and perhaps ERN numbers corresponding, that we would then in order not to add to the confusion that already exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: While we still have this document before us, Mr. Janic, the issue of handing over documents, let's touch upon that. This order, in fact, was sent to the unit of the special police within the police administration; however, it is addressed to the chief of that police administration, and then he refers it or forwards it to the commander of the special police. Was this the usual, regular, normal way it was done.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The coded orders from the Ministry of Interior would be sent to the police administration, and then they would forward it to the commander of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 65 ter 01812.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This order is somewhat different to the one that we've seen before. It's also of 22nd of July, issued by Mr. Markac, addressed to the Varizdin police administration, with a note that it should be delivered to the special police unit commander. And in the order, it is ordered that up until the 22nd of July, 1900 hours, they are to head with 120 members of the unit towards the Zadar-Knin police administration. Further on, there are deals about what the members of the special police should take with them. They should take short barrel and long barrel weapons; anti-armoured equipment, at least eight, for multiple uses; 24 anti-armour weapons for single use; protective equipment, flak jackets, helmets, combat kits, and sleeping bags. Speaks about equipment that is mentioned here, the equipment used by the special police, tell us, please, this is a lot of baggage to carry. How was this equipment transported?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the unit moved from its seat to the area of operation, they moved in a convoy of vehicles, and the equipment was moved in vehicles in that convoy; and in the area where the special police operated, all the equipment, the personal equipment, was carried by the men themselves. As for the equipment of logistical nature, there was a logistics department that organised the transport of that equipment using helicopter, trucks, and any other vehicles as required.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this document. I hope there are no problems with the translation with this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, I heard you saying, "No objection," is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You had not activated your microphone at that moment. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D540.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D540 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Can we now see document 65 ter 01811, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What we are going to see now is a slightly different order issued on the same date, that is, the 22nd of July, by Mr. Markac, addressed to the commander of the Special Unit through the chief of the Istria police administration. And it reads as follows: And with regard to carrying out the most complex tasks within the line of work of special police, on 24th of July, they shall have ready 100 members active and reserve servicemen, as well as one rocket artillery battery. It is also ordered that this level of readiness must guarantee a swift within two hours departure of all men to the site of the task. In the last paragraph of this order, it is particularly emphasised that during the going to the area of task and the use of vehicle, the unit has to travel in a convoy and adhere to traffic regulations. Mr. Janic, this is a slightly different order. Can you comment on it. This is an order to place reserve forces on the ready for a potential engagement in a mission.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Since the special police was in the area of Zadar, some other units, including the one from Zadar, was ordered to be on the ready, so that within a very short time, they can be on the move to the area where the special police battalion was. So these were the orders for stand-by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When special police units moves to the area of mission or back down regular roads, you already said that the common practice was to travel in a convoy of vehicles, as a whole. So this is in compliance with this order?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see from this order, even these details were provided, such as the maximum speed of the convoy, because a long convoy of official vehicles can cause traffic problems; and, also, there were obliged to adhere all traffic regulation, including speed limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, any objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D541, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D541 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One short question with regard to this, but we're now skipping to another topic. We are going to discuss check-points set up after the liberation of the occupied territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When a special police convoy properly marked was travelling down the road and came to a check-point, what was the regime of their passing the check-points manned by either the civilian police or the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police check-points manned by regular police or military police stopped vehicles at their own discretion. If there was a convoy of official vehicles, then they have the right of passage according to the traffic regulations that were in place then and now. Therefore, they did not have any need to stop such convoy. It had the right of passage in traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can now move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have, please, 65 ter 02118.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 23rd of July, which was also coded and addressed to the chiefs of two police administrations, Osijek Baranja and Sisak Moslovina; and it was to be delivered to the special police unit commanders within these PUs. It was signed by chief of department, Mr. Zeljko Sacic. The order reads that: "Immediately upon the receipt of this order," that is, on the 23rd of July, "each of you is to send one multiple rocket launcher, Rak 12, 128-millimetre with one BK, which stands for combat kit, and a crew; and they are to be send to the Zadar-Knin PU headquarters." Would you agree that this was one of the orders intended for reinforcing and replenishing the equipment of special police for their forthcoming tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. This order was sent to the special police units in Osijek and Sisak in order for it to be reinforced with artillery forces from the police in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We see that this order was signed Mr. Zeljko Sacic; and from an earlier document, we saw when the joint special police forces staff was formed that Mr. Sacic was appointed the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D542.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D542 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Mikulicic, I now noticed that VLR and VBR both are multiple rocket launchers. No problem with that. Okay. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Can we now please have 65 ter 01888.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Now, what we see here is that the joint forces were gradually being equipped with combat equipment and manpower. What followed, on the 29th of July, 1995, was an order issued by the Main Staff of the Croatian army, sent, as we can see here, to Mr. Mladen Markac, the commander of the Special Units. If we look at the next page, this order was signed by the chief of Main Staff, General Zvonimir Cervenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So the order was signed by the chief of Main Staff. It was sent encoded --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I only briefly saw the first page, but this does not appear to be the English translation of the Croatian document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's not. It's not. Now we have problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, a similar problem. I was still checking the previous one, where I do not actually, in the original, found yet the abbreviation "VBR," but I might be wrong there. This one is also suffering a bit, Ms. Mahindaratne, from creative composition of originals and translations.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have just sent an e-mail back to the trial support.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour, if this helps or further complicates the matter, but when I called it up in ring-tail, I seem to get the same document as I read the numbers on the -- that appear to the left. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will see what happened. I have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... as far as I can tell, I have the correct English translation of that document. No. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... what I have uploaded for various reasons. First of all the, handwritten annotation dated the 8th of June, 2004 does not appear in the translation, and it did appear in previous translations. Then I see that if only I look at the addressee, then I see an accused in another case appears, rather than an accused in this case. So, therefore, I have great doubts on whether this is a translation of the same document. Let's look at the numbers. That sometimes helps us out.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could assist. The same document from the document served on us last night by the Defence, the same document is at 65 ter 0 -- I'm sorry, 1892, and there the translation seems to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I think documents are admitted under their 65 ter or their Defence number; and if the translation which is directly attached to that document is not a translation of that document, then we have a problem. I don't think that we could accept that 65 ter number A is the original and 65 ter number B would be the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President that is not what I meant. I meant that this same document is listed under a different 65 ter number which is 1892; and under that, the translation seems to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I see that you have found a better matching original and translation. Then I suggest that we -- well, of course, I do not know which one then corresponds. Does it correspond with the original B/C/S document or does it correspond with the English translation, Ms. Mahindaratne?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we sort this perhaps after the break, because there are, I see, a whole lot of documents of the same document with different translations. I will be in a better position to assist Court if Mr. Mikulicic could postpone this particular document till after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that Judge Kinis will be happy that he wasn't here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, of course, this lack of precision in uploading documents really embarrasses the Defence who wants to use that material, Ms. Mahindaratne. So it is not one mistake but a whole series of mistakes. I also see that these two documents, which are not the same, they bear a same number in their heading; and, at the same time, the heading is not the same. For example, in the original, I see same class, same number; but then, for example, "Zagreb" appears not in the translation. So I don't know what actually has happened here. Mr. Mikulicic, it's a nuisance for you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- how to proceed. Is there any way that you could move to a subject which hopefully will not suffer from the same chaos.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to do so, but I must say that I could not predict what would be the obstacles for the other documents, because that is something out of my control. What I would like to suggest is that we can use the translation of this document, which is 65 ter 01892, but this translation is a little bit slightly different than the documents that I am using in original, and that only refers to the handwritten text on the bottom left-hand corner or the second page of the document. So we will show the original document on the screen, and I will point up on the signature and all other subject in those two versions are identical. So we could proceed with this because this document is very important for me. It is kind of [indiscernible] to another portion of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then with this proviso that the document shown in the original is not in every respect fully and accurately translated mainly, I do understand, in the field of handwritten additions. That is on the back of our mind. Please proceed. Could you check then now whether this is the document and this is the translation that you'd like to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janic, I apologise for these administrative delays in your testimony, but it is something we are facing every day. There are too many documents and mistakes do happen. This document is something that was issued by the Main Staff 'and if we look at the last page of the document, which is page 2, we will see that the document was issued by the chief of the Main Staff, General Cervenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We have a problem again, because this original -- this version in original Croatian text with the ERN number 949 is not the same that I have, and this is ERN three last digits 091 with a handwritten text on the bottom left corner. So, anyway, we could solve the problem, I suggest, by putting -- yes, this one is perfect. Okay. Finally. One more less. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janic, we can see that the document was signed by Mr. Cervenko, and I would like to draw your attention to the handwritten portion in the lower left corner where it says approved by deputy minister and there is a signature, and I suggest to you that it was Mr. Zjelko Dermanovic [phoen], the deputy minister who signed this. Can you reconfirm that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that this is the signature of the deputy minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We can also see that this order or this document was submitted to the commanders of the areas in Split and Gospic, and now let's go back to the first page of the document. First of all, let's try and locate the time when this document was issued. If you look at the overall picture of the security situation in the area, and I'm referring to the general area, would you agree with me that this was the time when Grahovo had been liberated in the neighbouring Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. Actually, this order preceded the operation, which, at the moment when it started, we called it Operation Storm; but up to then, we didn't know that was its name. And as can you see in the introductory part of this order, the security situation in the general area and the threat of Serb attack in Bosnia against the area of Bihac was the basis for issuing such an order and to launching this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So we're talking about the context of Operation Storm, and we can look at it in a general terms. And the general situation is fighting is that was going on in the neighbouring Bosnia-Herzegovina around the territory of Bihac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And now that we have located the order within a certain time-frame, let's move on to item number 1. Under 1 in this order, the MUP special forces are ordered to carry out an offensive from the operations based in the area of Mount Velebit and a precise location is described to take control of the area of Mali Golic, Sveti Rok, Gracac, and Prezid. Then under item 1, what needs to be done is to cut the Gospic-Gracac road between Sveti Rok and Stikada. Mr. Janic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These documents, even the content of them, apart from the handwriting, are not the tame, or at least one is not the translation of the other. Could I just take you to, for example, under point 2: "The operation shall be carried out ..." You see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there follows, in the first phase, apparently the first "etup"[phoen]. For example, I find in the original a number "934," which, apparently, is related to Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I'm trying to find that in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And that is not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is not there. So the content of this document is not the same, so I have great difficulties with proceeding with this document on the basis that, apart from the handwriting, it would be the same document. Therefore, I suggest that we have an early break now because, for the Chamber - I do understand the importance for you to proceed - but this is just a risky exercise we're doing at this moment. We are putting questions on one document. I saw other differences, for example, in the heading where the English says "Zagreb, 29th July 1995"; whereas, the original appears to say that it is the "29th of July, 1995," but at "12.00." So they are not the same. Even if the differences are minor, the Chamber cannot -- we do not have grip on where differences are. And if I can already identify a few of the these differences, then we really have to sort out these kind of things, and we can't continue on the basis of the assumption you just made. Ms. Mahindaratne, I am afraid you have a lot to explain, or at least a lot to settle, and how we will proceed after the break is unknown to me and will depend highly on what the parties are able to achieve in the next 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just suggest, we have got notice of 292 documents from the Defence last night; but, if for instance, Mr. Mikulicic could tell me the exact documents he plans to use during the next few hours, we could, during this 25 minutes, try to see that the translations are uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least you could prioritise those documents. And I take it that you're not revealing any Defence secrets. Ms. Mahindaratne will just look at the numbers, close her eyes, close her ears, and just try to find an administrative solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... will put a blanket over the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the record, what we just saw on our screen was a B/C/S document which was uploaded under 65 ter 01888, and we tried to match it with an English document which was uploaded under 65 ter number 01892. We resume at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you continue, there are two small issues on which I'd like to provide or seek clarification. The first one is about Prosecution Exhibit P53. That was marked for identification. I refer to the transcript pages 1357 and following. The problem at that time was that it was not uploaded in e-court. Ms. Mahindaratne, I raise it because you're here and it was Mr. Flynn's testimony. We then used another document on the ELMO; and, finally, it is perfectly clear what the document was. Now, since then, one way or the other, it disappeared from my eyes, and it doesn't appear now in the list of admitted exhibits. Now, it was never admitted, so to that extent that's fine. It doesn't appear anymore at all. P53 is now, again, uploaded. It is an order dated the 8th of August, 1995, issued by Ivan Cermak, three items. The first one that: "As of the 8th of August, all UNCRO elements," and that is from 1500 hours, "with clearly displayed insignia may move freely in the areas of Knin and Drnis." And, the third one, I read is that the order takes effect immediately. That document now is again back, it is admitted into evidence, and it is in the system now under P53.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's one issue. Mr. Tieger, there's another matter. The Chamber had some, although, information that there may be a gap in the testimony to be heard by videolink soon. If there would be a gap, then I think it would be appropriate that at least the Defence would be informed immediately. I don't know whether there is something to be confirmed in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think there is some concrete information we can provide the Defence, Your Honour, if I can do that at the break, so I -- I avoid any risk of misunderstanding. I don't think it assists them appreciably to get to get it now as opposed to an hour from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the Chamber - I don't know exactly by what means - at least receives information. It is about Witness 172, from what I understand. And it is something that the Chamber considers that the Defence should know if there's any truth in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I quite agree. And, of course, we had intended to notify everyone simultaneously. Had it not been for the flurry of activity that preceded the recent break, I would have done so at the recent break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we at this moment in an electronic environment in which we could proceed, Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Frankly, Your Honour, I don't know. We just exchanged information during the break with the Prosecution's office, and we supplied 65 ter numbers of the documents that we intend to use during further cross-examination. And we were told, maybe Ms. Mahindaratne could explain this, that they are doing their best to resolve the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have never seen Ms. Mahindaratne doing anything else. But, Ms. Mahindaratne, what's the result.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we hope that -- that everything will go off. We have a task force working on it right now. In fact, they have been working through the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see. The proof of the pudding is in the eating, Mr. Mikulicic, so let's give it a try.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will proceed with the document that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janic, let us now return to what we were discussing before the break. We've already mentioned the time-frame work of this document. Let's now look at item 1 of the document, which orders that special forces of the MUP should cut off the road Gospic-Gracac in the area of Sveti Rok and Stikada. Would you agree with me, Mr. Janic, that this road was one of the vital roads, strategically speaking, in that area at that time, in terms of the defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina because this road divided the occupied territory which was under the control of the Republic of Serbian Krajina into the northern and southern parts?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The Gracac-Gospic road was one of the key roads; and, in the end, it was one of the objectives of our operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Later on, this same road leads on to Otric. Could you confirm, please, that the same is true of that part of the road?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the roads that were in our area of responsibility were designated as very important and as objectives, so this also referred to the Gracac-Gospic, Obrovac-Gracac, Gracac-Otric, and Gracac-Udbina. All those roads were designated as strategic communication lines for which it was important to gain control over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to prevent the enemy to bring in reinforcements during the operation, in order to break up their defences, and in order to attain all the objectives of our operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In item 2 of this order, mention is made that the radio relay installation at Celavac should be taken. Could you please describe in a few sentences what type of installation that this was?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The radio relay was a vital significance for the Serbian forces because all communications of their army were -- went through this installation, and this is one of the vital strategic objectives that we had to put under our control in order to break up their communications and, thus, make our operation more feasible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Item 3, the pass and tunnel at Prezid. Could you please describe briefly what the significance of these was and -- for the operation, and also how important it was for the enemy forces, the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Operation Storm, this particular area, the Celavac and the tunnel and pass at Prezid, were, in fact, in the -- on the axis of our operation, and I can speak of it. These were strategic points. The pass and the tunnel at Prezid, this is the southern part of Mount Velebit. And, from this area, you could control the communication in the areas to the south of Velebit, in the area of Obrovac. And to the north, you could have control over the Gracac area, the area towards Gracac. So it was a strategically important point because it enabled control over -- an oversight of the entire territory there. So it was a strategic objective, a strategic goal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, was it to be expected that these strategic points would be defended by the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and that they were very much reinforced and fortified?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, the special police staff and the group that was preparing the operation, after receiving from the army and the intelligence service a full intelligence snapshot of the deployments of the enemy in that area, including at Celavac and Prezid, we knew very well, we were clear, and we had clear information that later -- as it later turned out were very correct. We even had aerial photos where you could see the deployment of the first line of defence of the enemy, which was on Mount Velebit, and also the second line, which was in front of the Celavac pass and tunnel. So there were two defence lines. They were fortified and defended with artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So there was a lot of fighting, fierce fighting in this area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that. On their forward defence line, at the Mali Alan pass, was the strongest fortification of the Serbian defence, and this was on the axis of our operation, of my operation, my mission. There were tens of fortified bunkers and artillery positions; and this is the area where a few days before Operation Storm, they had pulled in a lot of artillery and heavy artillery pieces. And in our area of responsibility, this was the area where the fiercest fighting occurred, and we suffered a lot of casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In item 4, order is issued to connect, to link up with the forces of the Split ZP, and order is made that -- an order is given that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the place names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, could you please repeat the place names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will repeat, yes, Your Honour. So this is Jasenica, J-a-c-e-n-i-c-a; then Zaton, Z-a-t-o-n; then Muskovci, M-u-s-k-o-v-c-i; and then Prezid, P-r-e-z-i-d. Could I proceed? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Further on, in item 2, the order is given to carry out this operation in two stages in a total of three days. Following this, more detail is given about the first stage, and it says that tactical surprise should be brought about by bringing in strong forces and strong artillery reinforcements, and that the front line -- the line should be -- a certain line should be reached. Perhaps you could describe briefly what the role of artillery support was, and how did that fit in with the operations?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the framework of Operation Storm, the special police had their own artillery that was deployed along the axis of attack, and the use of this artillery was twofold. Because the lie of the land was very difficult and our positions were below the Serbian defence positions in that area, it was impossible to attain the objectives of our operation without the use of artillery. So that in the first stage of the operation, as soon as the operation was launched at 5.00 a.m. on the 4th of August, our artillery, the artillery of the special police, struck the previously defined targets of the enemy in the area of Velebit, targets that were on their first lines of defence, and the enemy artillery that was deep in the rear of their positions. That was one way that our artillery was used in the operation. And the other employment -- the other type of employment was that when we commanded on certain axes of attacks and when we would reach a certain point which we could not capture without artillery support, I, as commander of the main axis of attack in this case, would call the artillery commander or the Chief of Staff, provide the targets, give their -- identify the targets, provide their coordinates to our forces. So our artillery forces were used in this way only.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the second page of this order where the second stage is described of this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It is ordered that, by bringing in the main forces, the attack should continue until a certain line is reached and then place names are given there. And under 1, it says that the radio relay installation at Celavac should be ceased. We have already mentioned this. So the pass and the tunnel at Prezid should be captured. We have also mentioned that, and that they should link up with the forces of the 9th Guards Brigade. In item 3, it says that the remainder of the forces should be employed for an act of defence; and in the event of a positive tactical situation, they should carry out an offensive in order to endanger the Medak-Sveti Rok road. This what the road that we mentioned before, the one leading from Gracac to Gospic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In item 4, it says that during preparations and conduct of combat operations, work should be coordinated with the command of the Split ZP and the Gospic ZP Military District. Tell us briefly, what was the relationship or what was the role of the special police unit with -- and what was their connection or their relation with these two Military Districts?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special police in this operation coordinated their work with these areas -- with these Military Districts because we had our own area of responsibility. To the left, we had Gospic; and to the right, we had the area of responsibility of Split. So the forces on the left and right flanks of us had to coordinate this operation, and we coordinated our work throughout the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did the special police forces, at any point in time, were they in a position to carry out the commands or orders either from the Military District of Split or that of Gospic?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, we carried out the orders of the Main Staff of the Croatian army, exclusively the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In item 5, it is ordered that the forces would carry out the task by -- must be ready by 1st August 1995, at 0400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have this document assigned a number, once a translation -- the proper translation is provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I then take it that we worked on the basis of the B/C/S version and that the right translation still has to be found, to be attached. Under those circumstances, I would suggest that we mark the B/C/S version which apparently was 01888.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mark that for identification. And the Chamber would like to be informed explicitly and also would like see hard copies of at least this document, so that we can satisfy ourselves that we're dealing with the right document. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number D543, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In preparation for the operation --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we please have document 02164.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In preparation for the operation, the joint special police forces need to be properly trained. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We see the document on our screens now, which is dated 30th of July, 1995. It was sent by Mr. Mladen Markac to the chief of Main Staff of the Croatian army, asking for reinforcement and assistance for special police forces by placing at their disposal one ME-8 helicopters, two helicopters with crew as well, and to approve the use of another helicopter for the period of six days. The purpose was to ensure continuing logistical support due to the configuration of the ground at Velebit. As far as you can remember, did you get these helicopters?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If you look at page 2 of this document, we can see that the special police sector had problems with their own helicopters because some of them had to be repaired and others were damaged, and that was the reason why this request was sent to the Main Staff. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was precisely the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have the number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D544, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D544 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see document 02159, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In addition to the replenishment procedure with these helicopters, Mr. Markac, on the same date, 30th of July, requested ammunition replenishment and other necessary material required for the carrying out of the operation. We're going to see this right now on the screens. What is requested here are rockets, shells, all kinds of ordnance and ammunition. As far as you can remember, was that the way how the joint forces were supplied with appropriate equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. I remember this request which helped reinforce our forces. Our assessment of the logistical support necessitated this kind of replenishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can I please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D545, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D545 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Earlier you mentioned -

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the meantime, if we could please have document 00811 pulled up on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that certain intelligence was gathered about the enemy that was to be targeted by this operation. We're now going to see a document issued by the internal control department of the special police sector, which precisely speaks about their continuing reconnaissance missions and gathering of information and intelligence. In the second paragraph, it says: In my regular contacts with Mr. Vranjkovic in the village of Modric where we reviewed the situation related to reconnaissance by our units in the Velebit area (our zone of responsibility), I received regular reports gathered from our reconnaissance and operations groups, and I forwarded summaries thereof to the commander of our joint forces, Mr. Zdravko Janic." Mr. Janic, do you recall that this was the methodology applied in preparation in terms of intelligence work?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly so. Our intelligence department, or internal control, gathered intelligence; and as you can see from this report, he conveyed this information to me as the commander of the joint forces in order for me to have access to all the information in the event of any operation being launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Are we talking now about Mr. Miljenko Vranjkovic from the internal control department?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is our deceased colleague Mr. Vranjkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You knew him very well?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We closely cooperated since the early 1990s until the late 1990s until he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D546.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D546 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: To save some time, Your Honour, I have a couple of documents that are on the very same subject as this one, and maybe we could just briefly go through them and tender into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it your intention to tender them from the bar table? Is Ms. Mahindaratne informed about which documents they are?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No. No, she is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: She is not. Well, then, you may have to go through it very briefly. Of course, if you tender them from the bar table, of course, you could still do that, but then, of course, you're at risk that there comes an objection. And if you inform Ms. Mahindaratne well in advance, then, of course, she could make up her mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will go very briefly through the documents. [Interpretation] Can we now please have document 01885.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Another document issued by the internal control dated 29th of July. It says that the UN forces were on a red alert, that the enemy has fortified the forward line and having carried out defensive engineer work and planted mines, that these reports have been presented to you, and that there is panic among enemy ranks because of the successes of the Croatian army in Bosnia. Mr. Janic, did you have, at the time, any information that the army of the -- of the Serbian Republic of Krajina that there was an imminent attack prepared by the army of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Already at that time, and that was the 29th of July, it was obvious that both sides were going to face a decisive movement particularly as a result of the success of the Croatian army in the operations in Bosnia, which had a great strategic impact on the position of the Serbian forces in the so-called Serbian Krajina. Their position and -- their defence positions were considerably weakened as a result of our operations in Bosnia, and it was clear to everyone that the moment was approaching due to these tactically favourable circumstances for Croatia to probably undertake an operation for the liberation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D547, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D547 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have the document 02192 pulled up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In line with what you just told us, Mr. Janic, we have another document from the internal control dated the 3rd of August, which is practically just immediately before the operation. It seems that the Serbian army has started fortifying their positions; and that during the day, it was observed that a convoy with 19 trucks and six buses with around 300 troops, a tank, five mortars, a truck with mounted mortars, two field kitchens, four field guns, and an ambulance were travelling. The internal control also noticed -- the internal control of the special police also noticed that in the area of Gracac, buses with some 50 troops were seen heading southwards, and a truck full of ammunition. Their destination was Mali Alan where 60 troops and another vehicle with some 12 troops were seen. It also says, here, that in the area of Korenica in the south, also movements of trucks with tarpaulin were noticed, with troops, and two T-55 tanks, one armoured personnel carrier, and a convoy of 12 buses with between 400 and 500 soldiers. This information clearly indicates that the army of the Republika Srpska [as interpreted] was receiving reinforcement both in manpower and in equipment. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had this intelligence, and we had this information as stated here. We even had more information. In the two days preceding Operation Storm, the Serbs had fortified their positions and brought in artillery and tanks; therefore, it was obvious that they had a hunch of what our intentions were and that we were going to launch an operation for liberation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, just one piece of advice. If I don't ask you for a broader explanation, please keep your answers brief because we are time pressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D548.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D548 is admitted into evidence. I have, however, one issue, yes. I heard in the translation that you said that it was an indication that the army of the Republika Srpska [as interpreted]. That's what I heard. But I know see in the transcript that something is missing, so I take it that you were referring to the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have document 03515, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is another document issued by the internal control department compiled on the 28th June, 1995, which means that was before the operation itself was launched. It deals, in a way, with what kind of forces the army of Republika Srpska [as interpreted] has at its disposal. It was addressed to General Cermak and to the chief of the sector, later the chief of the staff of special police, Zeljko Sacic. This is an intelligence assessment of the enemy forces in the area of responsibility of the joint police forces in the area of Velebit on the eve of the forthcoming operation, which was aborted, as we had said before. We're not going to go through the entire document now. I would just like to draw your attention to the table on page 2, which shows the strength and the equipment that the enemy can potentially engage in the area of responsibility of special police. The anticipation is around 1.000 troops, 15 tanks and nine APCs, and a number of artillery guns, which, due to unclear reasons, is not indicated in the last column. If we now move to page 3 of this document, we will see that these forces could later be reinforced by bringing another 880 troops, 12 tanks, six APCs, and 15 artillery guns, two of which would be multiple rocket launchers. It also says that the enemy forces carrying out defence operations on the Sveti Alan-Mali Rok --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number of weapons in the last section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please repeat the number at the request of the interpreters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the last table anticipates that the enemy on the Sveti Rok-Mali Alan defence line may deploy 620 troops, nine tanks, six APCs, and nine artillery guns. And, finally, there is mention of the possibility that the enemy, which is the army of Serbian Krajina, can expect to have air support from MiG-21 and J-21 aircraft, as well as from Gazelle helicopters. Mr. Janic, this data depicts an intelligence situation which later turned out to be rather accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that this intelligence analysis was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D549, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D549 is admitted into evidence. Nevertheless, I have one question to you, Mr. Mikulicic, which is the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that something was missing in one of the tables for unknown reasons to you, which tends to be giving evidence that what is not in the table nevertheless was there. What's the basis for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Well the basis is that on the table on page 2, the first line says that there are nine cannons, guns. The line 2 says there are nine and line 3 says there is are nine, but all together there is not specific number, and I counted 3 times 9 is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: -- is 27, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And could you take me back to the portion where you said you found the basis. That's on page?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It is on page 2 of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: -- on the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at this moment at the English translation. Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. The English translation is there, page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 4. Let me just check that. Where do you then find that there should be another number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Well, it says that the 9th Motorised Brigade of the 1st Battalion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, for the total, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the total.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I now see what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Obviously, someone who is writing this table --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has forgotten to add them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see document D5-2-0, 520.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We now had a look at document that the intelligence assessment of the department of the internal control of the special police, and you said that, in fact, this assessment proved to be reliable. Now we can see a document before us that comes from the archives of the enemy, the enemy's archives, the army of the Serbian Krajina. It is a combat report dated 9th of August, 1995. The commander forwarded this to the 7th corps commander, Captain First Class Radivoj Paravanja. And in this document, events are described, as well as the forces that the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina had engaged in combat that commenced on the 4th of August at 5.00 in the morning. I don't want to go through the entire document, but I would like to draw your attention to page 2 of this document, where it is stated -- or where reference is made to the equipment that was withdrawn from the combat area. It also mentions equipment that was left there, equipment destroyed, and so on and so forth. In item 2, it says that equipment was withdrawn, and hen you have Howitzers, 76-millimetre guns, 76-millimetre gun ZIS mortar, light rocket launcher, 128-millimetre light rocket launcher, 82-millimetre mortar. And then under item 2.2, reference is made to the equipment left in the field. We have heard evidence according to which certain military equipment was noticed by UN observers. It had been left in the direction of Srb in Bosna [as interpreted]. Then reference is made to tanks APCs, to an artillery piece. In 2.3, reference is made to destroyed equipment or ordnance, three artillery pieces or guns; 2.4 refers to other kinds of military equipment; and item 2.5 refers to depots, ammunition depots: An ammunition depot in Krupa which was destroyed; quarter master depot in Zegar that was destroyed in combat; a depot on Velebit also destroyed. And then in Zegar, there was a hospital. Mr. Janic, do you know anything about depots that were found on your axis of action and that belonged to the former army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were warehouses in my direction of action, and in the course of the operation there were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Very well. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 01641. I hope there won't be any problems with the version of the document -- with this version of the document. It is a document dated 5th of August, issued by the chief of the Main Staff, Zvonimir Cervenko --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, the previous document we saw --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was already admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that I have seen it, but you have, as far as -- did you refer to the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Exhibit number D520.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see, yes. I apologise for not being attentive enough. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This document which is up on the screen is an order from General Cervenko dated the 5th August, and this order refers to the continuation of combat in D Plus 1. That is the second day of the operation. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So, here, the order is that the combat, on the 5th of August, must commence in accordance with the orders and decisions of the military positions, posts, or districted. "HRM," that is an abbreviation for the Croatian navy?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: "HRZ" is an abbreviation for the Croatian air force?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: "JB," could you help me with that, please. Perhaps that means the southern battlefield?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps. I'm not familiar with such an abbreviation, though.
