utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And it also refers to special MUP units?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now move on to page 2, item 3.5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is an order that refers to the MUP Special Units, and the order is that an energetic attack and manoeuvre should be launched to seize the settlement of Gracac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And, later, we will see that this was attained. We will go into more detail later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D550, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D550 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We're just checking translation, Your Honour. I think there has been some misunderstanding. Mr. Misetic reminds me that in the English translation the abbreviation "JB" was translated as "javna bezbednost," which means public security. And this is obviously not the abbreviation in this document, but we could check it afterwards, not to spend much time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. And if there is any need to have the translation to be corrected, please, after having consulted with the Prosecution, to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... not to waste time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see P583 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, we'll seen have this document up on the screen. Mr. Markac issued this document in the staff in the command Seline. Just an introductory question. The headquarters -- the Seline headquarters is mentioned as the place where this was issued. Can you tell us what this is about, please, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a HQ in Seline, and General Markac was there. The operations HQ that conducted operations in the tactical sense said the direct conduct of operations was conducted from HQ in Velebit itself. So that would be the main HQ, but the main operations HQ was on Velebit. That's where operations in the field in the tactical sense were conduct the from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And an additional explanation. Where is Seline?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It at the foot of Velebit. It is to the south of Velebit on the southern side of Velebit, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Very well. So this was forwarded to the chief of the Main Staff. It was a report on lines that had been attained by the collective forces of the special police. And it says that on the 5th of August at 5.00, these joint forces commenced with artillery preparations and started targeting Seline, Gracac, Lovinac, Velika, and Mali Zuljine and the depth of the territory. And afterwards at 8.00, these joint forces liberated Lovinac. At 9.30, they seized dominant elevations around Gracac and created the preconditions for liberating Gracac by carrying out a manoeuvre around Resnick. At the time, by using forces of the strength of one battalion they break up the second enemy line on Velika and Mali Zuljine. And preconditions were created to advance in the direction of the Celavac facility. At the same time, enemy forces were driven back along the Sveti Rok-Papuca axis. Mr. Janic, as far as direction towards Celavac is concerned, you said that was your direction. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm the precision of this report with regard to the lines attained, and I can also confirm the reliability of this information since I was in command of that battalion that attained the second enemy line at Velika and Mali Zuljine. So I can personally confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see P584.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This document is a similar one. On the 5th of August, Mr. Markac reported to the chief of the Main Staff and informed him of the fact that by 11.30, special police forces on the 5th of August took full control of Gracac; and by 12.00, took control of the facilities Celavac and Prezid. Furthermore, it is stated that on that day, on the 5th of August, they attained the Drenova Glava-Korac-Ajdukovic line. The report also states that they, thus, fully carried out the task assigned to the joint forces of the special police, and forces were being regrouped. And these forces, in accordance with your order - reference is made to the chief of the Main Staff, to whom this report was forwarded - it is said that with these forces, they would continue with the attack on the main Gracac-Bruvno axis and on the other auxiliary axis, Gracac-Malivan. And logistical was being provided to units. Can you confirm that these dates and these periods of time are correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm that the time of dates and the information that this report contains is precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, we are now looking at P584, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the witness testified it was an accurate report. What is the use exactly of going through it again, and then asking whether the details in there are correct? He already said that it was an accurate report. Similar thing about 583.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would just like to emphasise the specific time-frame in which the part of the operation has been conducted, and that it refers to some position of the defence as it regards to events that were follow-up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But on the basis of what the witness testified, I mean, we're not here to seek further emphasis by witnesses. This is an clear, a clear statement he said: "Is that a correct and accurate report." "Yes, it is." So, therefore, we know that the witness considers this is to be accurate information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. I maybe go into unnecessary details. I will take your guidance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Could we now see 02008, which is a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will soon see an order issued by General Cervenko dated the 6th August, in which the operation borders or operative limits of the area of responsibility are being determined between Military Districts, and the following is stated. When reference is made to competence or responsibility for Military Districts, would you agree that one is dealing with a military and territorial responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So this is a division of Military Districts in -- in an administrative sense. It has to do with a territorial responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Very well. In item A, an order is issued. And it says that between the Split Military District and the Gospic Military District, the dividing line should be represented by Mali Alan, Gracac, Velko Sedlo, Medjedak, and the Una railway station. This includes the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D551.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D551 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Can we see D281 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 280.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will now see a map, Mr. Janic. It will take a little time for it come up on the screen. This is a map that has already been admitted into evidence in this case. And, in fact, it represents the dividing lines between the Split and Gospic Military Districts, and this has been marked in blue. Could you confirm that we are, in fact, dealing with areas where operations were conducted, and can you tell us in which areas the special police units were engaged in operations, with reference to this map, naturally?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. I'll just have a quick look at the map. Yes. Most of the special police operations followed the Velebit-Gracac axis. That was a strategically important cross-roads at the village of Bruvno in the direction of Donji Lapac -- or rather, the state border by Kulen-Vakuf. So that was the entire axis of action for the special police unit. Mostly, they were present in the area of responsibility of the Military District of Gospic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will go into more detail a little later on with regard to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 01974, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What we will see now is an order from General Cervenko relating to combat operations on the third day of the operation, which means D Plus 2. The order is dated 6th August 1995, and I would like to refer you to item 2, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please scroll down the Croatian version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Item 2, last paragraph, also in the English version, where it says that parts of forces should capture Udbina from the direction of Ljubovo and continue their attack with the participation of the special units of the MUP, in order to capture Donji Lapac and reach the border between the area of Medjedak railway station at the Una river. So this refers to the Gospic area, and that is just what you told us about, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Item 3, on page 2 of the English version, relates to the special units of the MUP, and it is stated here --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's wait for the English version. Let's wait for the Croatian version, that as on page 2. I can see that the English version is already all right. Now we have the second page of the B/C/S -- Croatian version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It says here that the special MUP units, once they have captured the Bruvno and Malovan passes, should continue along the axis -- in the direction of Donji Lapac and capture the area, in coordination with the forces from the Military District of Gospic on the left flank and the forces of the Military District of Split on the right flank. This is consistent with what you know about this operation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number assigned to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D552, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D552 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 65 ter 01949.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will now see an order by General Cervenko relating to D Plus 3, in other words, the fourth day of Operation Storm. The order is dated 6 August 1995? In item 1, it is ordered that, by 1800 hours, the entire territory should be captured and the state border reached as ordered earlier. In item 2, it says that the commanders of the Split and Gospic Military Districts and the commander of special units of the MUP are duty-bound to coordinate the time of attack on the axis indicated, and that they should file a report on it and report to the Chief of Staff himself promptly. Mr. Janic, this order was carried out, as far as you can recall, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D553, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D553 is admitted into evidence. Could I ask you, Ms. Mahindaratne, to what extent is there any dispute, as far as you are concerned, about whether these were the orders given in Operation Storm and that Operation Storm developed --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: None, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in accordance with those orders and those lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: None, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Mikulicic, I am asking myself what we're doing. Of course, I see the importance of knowing who was there, of course, mainly, and in terms of locations where crimes allegedly were committed, and what the command structures were. But I think we go now in quite some detail as the development of the military operation, which, of course, is not without relevance, but it is not the core of this case. This case is not about how well or how badly or how, what, to some extent, how organised Operation Storm developed. But the details on who was instructed to go to what cross-roads and whether they were successful in getting the cross-roads, and then move on the next day, of course, we spend a lot of time on that. Just as we spent, for example, a lot of time on reading all of the names of people who were assigned. I will never hear perhaps of those people anymore. Let's try to focus on what really is the core of the case and what this witness could bring in that respect. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will, of course, follow your guidance, but just to stress that this witness is probably the only one who could explain from a very authorative position that, while he was part of this operation, how it was conducted. So we are trying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But we have the documents and Ms. Mahindaratne says it is not in dispute. So, of course, you can repeat that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you. [Interpretation] Could we now please pull up document P585.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is a report submitted by Mr. Markac to the Chief of Staff, where he describes how the operations line was attained and the operation carried out. And what I would like to know, from this document, is about the areas of Donji Lapac and Gornji Vakuf. It says here that in the early morning hours, on the 7th of August, the special police left Bruvno towards Udbina where it linked up with the forces of the 9th Brigade. That is in Gospic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And that those special police forces at 1900 hours captured Kulen-Vakuf and deployed on dominant features. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When they reached Kulen-Vakuf and took up dominant positions, this practically meant that the special police have completed their mission in Operation Storm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, once the line was reached, what happened? What did the special police do and what happened with their mission?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of 9th of August, after all the operations were completed, our units, which were in the area near the border with Bosnia at Gornji Vakuf, they were rotated, a Posavina brigade came and relieved our men, the joint forces were disbanded, and the units just went back to their original police administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So, in fact, this means that the special police units returned from the field after a mission. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, we discussed the special police commands in Seline and a point on the Velebit mountain. However, once Gracac was liberated, an area was established in Gracac where a small special police unit was deployed. Could you tell us a bit about this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When Gracac was liberated and because the conditions in the town were better than the previous conditions we had on Mount Velebit, a headquarters of the special police was established, and the chief of the staff, at that time the chief of the sector of the special police was its commander, and he commanded this staff up until the end of Operation Storm; and after Operation Storm, he commanded the activities that followed in its wake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when was this staff or this headquarters established in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was set up immediately, I think on the 5th of August in the afternoon. As soon as Gracac was captured, this headquarters was established there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether on this same day a police station was set up in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I've already mentioned that there was a regular police unit at the ready for each town, and their role was to establish a police station once those towns were liberated. So, in Gracac, on the 5th, immediately following the special police, a regular police unit entered Gracac and established a police station by placing the insignia of the Croatian police on the former police station and established a police administration and a police station there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us in a few sentences how this headquarters operated in Gracac, as compared to the previous -- its previous operations. Describe what the conditions in which it worked were.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you mentioned the headquarters -- when mention is made of headquarters, what we usually imply is they were well equipped with all kinds of equipment; but, in fact, this was very modest. We just had a computer, a radio station, and a couple of men sitting there. There was a map on the wall. So the conditions were really rather modest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that one of the persons who were there at the Gracac headquarters was Miljenko Gracac [as interpreted], whom we mentioned a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. At this time, on the eve of Operation Storm, he was involved in gathering of intelligence. And he -- he produced security assessments, and he was the one who spent most of his time at the headquarters. One could say that, at the time when the chief of the headquarters was not there, the Chief of Staff, he was the who actually ran the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was he the person who compiled and prepared daily reports that were submitted to the military -- war staff of the Croatian army within and which were sent via a special system?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He received and collected reports, and then he compiled them and prepared a report for the Main Staff of the Croatian army. He was the person in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to how these reports were sent? Technically speaking, how were they sent from Gracac to the military staff?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an electronic mail system which was encoded, and I know that we received a system -- one system of that type in order to be able to encode our messages and promptly inform thereof the Main Staff of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was this system referred to as the Rebus system?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The duties that Mr. Vranjkovic carried out in terms of encoding messages and so forth, these were tasks that were outside his normal scope of work of internal control, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that. Commanders were with their units, and he, at this point and in some situations, took on some commanding responsibilities in commanding the staff itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers. We've said that once the positions at Kulen-Vakuf were reached, the special police began to withdraw to their original police administrations. One portion of the special police or one number of special police officers also withdrew via the Gracac staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Units withdrew using various axes, and some returned to Gracac where they had been deployed earlier. Sometimes, they returned to the Lugari base. They returned to various areas where they stayed for a while, where they picked up their equipment, and then went back to their original basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that once Gracac was liberated and special police units moved on in the direction of Kulen-Vakuf, that part of the equipment remained at the headquarters in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Each of our units was accompanied by a logistics units, and as we advanced, the logistics department carried all the equipment, both individual and collective, all equipment that the unit had its disposal. They transported it for the unit and deployed it in various base camps used by the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned earlier that this type of equipment was transported by trucks.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By trucks, buses, also by vehicles that were used to transport men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have D295.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You will now see a photo that was taken on the 8th of August, 1995, in Gracac and introduced into evidence in these proceedings. The photograph was taken by a witness who testified here. This is a truck, and I would like to ask you to identify this truck based on its plates. Could you tell us whom this truck belonged to?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the plates, 010, these are the plates that were used by all units of the Ministry of the Interior in their seat and they were also used by the special police units. For instance, the special unit in Dubrovnik also had plates starting with the digits 010.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please describe briefly what we can see on this front part of the truck. We can see a plate with some Cyrillic inscription on it and we can see some antlers. Could you tell us what this means?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. After the operation was completed this meant that our country was liberated from -- and relieved from occupation and people then picked up street signs and picked up, as it were, trophies in order to express their joy because the war had ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is this a truck that was used for transporting logistical equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Personnel was not transported in trucks. We rode in all-terrain vehicles. Trucks of this type were used for logistical support.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see Exhibit P325.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In this photograph you can see two members that you identified as those of special police. No, can we see the next photograph, please. Okay. We can look at this photograph for just a second. In the right-hand side you can see this blue truck that you said belonged to the police but we also can see a white Land Rover. Can you tell us -- can you identify this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can identify both vehicles. They were our vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next photograph, please, from the same body of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, could we ask the witness where I think that he said that these were not -- well, perhaps on the basis of this one, whether he could positively identify who are shown in the photograph. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So you can confirm that we see two people here and that they are members of the special police?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you maybe know their names?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In the background we see a building. Can you confirm that this is where the special police staff was headquartered?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not 100 percent sure, but I think that is the municipality of Gracac, and that this is the building where the special police staff was headquartered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We see a yellow bus here with a red ribbon or red tape. Do you recognise this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this was precisely the vehicle used by members of special police to be transported to their original units?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Given the large number of people who were gathered in one place for the sake of the operation and that there was a shortage of vehicles, we would rent vehicles from the town transport company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You have identified this building as the municipal hall, and we see that it's not damaged by any artillery attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. President, I think the witness said, I think this is the building. There was no confirmed identification. However, the question is phrased on the basis of --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, Mr. Mikulicic, there's a difference between we see that it is not damaged and we do not see that it is damaged. Could you make that distinction please and please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of your recollection of the days spent in Gracac, can you tell us what was the situation in town? Were there -- was there any damage on the buildings? Just in a couple of sentences.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since -- after I reached the road near Prezid, I entered Gracac and I can confirm that the town was intact, there was no damage caused by artillery. There was no immediate fighting over this particular town. Therefore, that there was no reason and I know that near the town there were some military depots that were legitimate targets but the town itself wasn't. And there was no fighting inside it and there were no artillery strikes targeting the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You said that you came across some army depots. Can you tell us where they were located?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember now. It was very near Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move on. Can we now see document number 02313.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The document that we are about to see on our screens is a summary report issued to Dr. Franjo Tudjman, the president of the Republic of Croatia, by the chief of Main Staff. The president of the republic is advised and informed about Operation Storm. The president of the republic was also the commander in chief of the armed forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't go into details of this report. What I would like to highlight are two aspects, and for that purpose can we please have page 4 in Croatian. It says here that the losses sustained by the Croatian army was 190 killed, 900 wounded and 14 missing. It also says that some combat equipment was either damaged or destroyed. And on page 5 in the Croatian version also some war booty was seized during the operation; for example, four aircraft -- another two aircraft, helicopters, et cetera. We needn't go my further details. Mr. Janic, are you aware that certain materiel was captured by our units?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Even we, on our axis of operation, managed to capture a significant amount of equipment such as tanks, guns, rockets, and depots. There was a lot of ammunition and equipment and weaponry seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, while you were advancing towards Otric and further beyond to Lapac and Gorni Vakuf, did you see the damaged and abandoned vehicles beside the road, and equipment as well?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. On each of these roads, while we were advancing during the operation, we saw broken vehicles or destroyed vehicles and weapons that were left behind while they were fleeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you notice, particularly at road junctions, any traces of firing from artillery? And I mean tanks and guns. Did you see any shell casings by the road while you were travelling towards Otric and further beyond towards Lapac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On several places, we saw traces of their artillery positions. We found empty shells after they had been firing from artillery and that happened on several occasions along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D554.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D554 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Mikulicic, we had a bit of a different schedule this morning. We had a very early break, so, therefore, this second break should start at least a bit earlier as well. But before taking the break, could you give us any indication on how much time you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would say like this. Having in mind what you have been said before the beginning of the testifying of this witness, I will try to finish my cross-examination, let's say, until 1.20, 1.25. So another -- an another -- an hour, let's say, I will spend on my cross-examination. And that said, and having in mind I just have to stress that I have been correcting my previous plan and that -- I finish a little bit earlier than I originally supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I hear from the other parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We don't have any questions for the witness, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We have no questions either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, from what you have heard until now could you give us an estimate on how much time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, we'll then have a break until 12.30. You will then have time until 20 minutes past 1.00. That would give you another 50 minutes, therefore, which would bring your total to five hours and 20 minutes, as matters stand now. Then we will try to do our utmost best to finish the testimony of this witness today. We adjourn, and we resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can we please now have document 01290.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: What are you going to see now is the document containing an analysis of Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: For the Chamber, the document that will be seen shortly is from 26th November 2001. But, in fact, there's another document from 1992, which is completely identical. This one is obviously some kind of retype of the document from 1992, but the document from 1992 has no translation. Although of both documents, the one that I will be showing, it's from 2001, and has translation, and I will suggest to admit it into evidence shortly. 1995, I'm sorry. I must correct myself. I mentioned the wrong year. I was thinking of 1995, not 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just assist. Both these documents, the 1995 document and 2001 document, were subject of the bar table submissions, so they already in, if that assists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We work on the basis that they will be admitted and we certainly do not expect you to object against admission.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Mikulicic, then you could work on the basis that they are in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is anything specific you would like further to elicit from the witness, of course, you can do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Then I will skip this document. This is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janic, we mentioned an analysis of the entire Operation Storm. Can you tell us in one or two sentences what your role was in the drawing up of this analysis, if any?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an analysis of Operation Storm. It was compiled by the chief of special police sector on the basis of the reports received from all units involved in Operation Storm, or rather, reports forwarded by axis commanders in our area of responsibility. Consequently, my report, as the commander of the main axis in Operation Storm, was an integral part and was incorporated into this analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at document number 2200, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This document is actually a war log kept at the Main Staff and in which all the events relating to Operation Storm were entered, pertaining to the period between 3rd August and 31st of October. Of course, we are interested in the first four days of Operation Storm. I would just like to point out that, for example, on page 2 of this war log, which bears the date 4th of August, 1995, and then after that, we can see reports from General Markac, the commander of the special police, about what was happening on the ground. In order to save time, we're not going to go through all these entry. I will just mention the one at 04.35 hours, where Markac called to say that the situation was regular. And after that, he called again the Main Staff, which was recorded here under item 38. That was at 0455 hours, and he said that special MUP units had set off according to plan, and so on and so forth. Mr. Janic, would you agree with me that that indicates that Mr. Markac was in permanent contact with the Main Staff of the Croatian army and was reporting about what was going on, on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to have this document admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D555.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D555 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us just take glance another at this analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It shows that a large depot in Sveti Rok and Boricivac [phoen] barracks were found with large quantities of ammunition and weapons. Can you confirm these findings?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm that these depots were, indeed, found containing a large quantity of equipment and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can proceed now. The special police unit is heading towards Lapac. Yesterday, you have seen the document P586, but I don't need to have it pulled up. This document was issued by Mr. Bolej [phoen], and it mentions that on the 7th of August, during the liberation of Donji Lapac by the joint forces, logistical support arrived at around 1600 hours. There was no major fighting in Donji Lapac, and that only two houses were on fire, as a result of artillery fire. After that, it says that a units of the Croatian army entered --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to slow down, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the testimony was not two by three, including the police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not referring to the testimony, but to the document P586.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will try do to slowly, but, you know, the time is pressing me. I feel it on my back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janic, that is when incidents in the town happened; houses wer set ablaze, they were shooting, et cetera. Now I'm going to show you a document which bears the number P111. It's an UN observers report for Sector South, relating to the 7th of August, 1995. This document has already been admitted into evidence in this case, and I would like to refer you to page 574 of this document, containing the observations made by the Jordanian battalion deployed near Gracac. It says that, on the 7th of August at 0745 hours, 15 Croatian army soldiers entered Uzlapic and set off towards Nabusi. The comment made was that the Croatian army was moving towards the border of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And after that, at 0835 hours, the report says that there was artillery fire opened on Donji Lapac by the Croatian army in Udbina. And the comment was that, apparently, Udbina was liberated and taken over by the Croatian army, and that they were preparing further attacks on Donji Lapac from there. Mr. Janic, do you remember this artillery fire on the morning of the 7th of August, which was targeting Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The fire came from Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Towards the bottom of the page, it says that, at 1335 hours, there was fierce shelling of Donji Lapac. Mr. Janic, at what time did special police enter Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around noon. I'm not exactly sure, and we can check it in reports. But we definitely were in the town when this fierce shelling took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How do you explain that while you were in town the Croatian army shelled Lapac from the direction of Udbina? Did they have information according to which you were in Lapac?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as we understood situation at the time, given the information I had received from the HQ, unfortunately they weren't aware of the fact that they were in Donji Lapac, or rather, that we had entered Donji Lapac before they had. And I remember that order from the chief of the Main Staff, D Plus 2, in which it was ordered that there should be coordination. This obviously was not coordinated effectively, and they were not aware of the fact that we had already entered Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: At the time, there was this incident of so-called friendly fire. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the following document, 3D00-1451.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We'll see the document up on the screen in a minute. It is a report that you drafted yourself, Mr. Janic. And you forwarded it to the chief of the sector Mr. Sacic. It is on the events in Lapac at the time, and I'd like to ask you about the following. Were you aware of the fact that the commander of the 118th Brigade, in the course of the combat for Donji Lapac, was killed, and there were a lot of casualties in that brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't testify that that home guards brigade -- I didn't know reasons for this at the time. I didn't know reasons for such conduct at the time. Later, however, I found out that in combat before Donji Lapac on their axis of action, they had suffered significant casualties. About 15 soldiers as well as the brigade commander were killed. Obviously, at that time, the chain of command wasn't functioning properly, in my assessment. That is my personal assessment of the situation that I observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Very well. And in light of the document that we have on the screen, you mention the fact that there were things that could not be tolerated, burning, shooting from the Croatian army. You spoke about the fact that Colonel Vranjkovic -- and at the end of the report, you say that the special police units were already outside the sphere of Donji Lapac when that happened, and they didn't participate in shooting or burning of any kind. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I would like an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D556.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now move on to another subject, and we will try to deal with it expeditiously, although it is very important. It has to do with searching the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, after the operation was concluded, you said that the special police units withdrew; however, you were soon involved in searching the terrain in the Petrova Gora area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the following document, 02314, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We'll see it's an order from the -- from the Main Staff. It says that special police units, under the command of General Markac, should clear the terrain and seize the Petrova Gora area, and then further details follow. You can see the order, Mr. Janic, which is dated 10th August. You started searching the Petrova Gora area. Before doing so -- or rather, in the course of doing that, did you come across members of the enemy forces? Did you discover any explosive devices? How long did this search last?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It lasted for two days. In our assessment in the area, enemy forces that had been dispersed were still present. They had not been organised. These groups had not been organised. But in the course of the -- of combing the terrain, there were no clashes. There was no contact with the enemy forces; however, we did find a lot of the equipment, weapons, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D557, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D557 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw that the special police units went to the Sector South area; and in that area, there were no special forces. However, given the needs that prevailed at the time, it was necessary to continue searching the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the following documents, 1414.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We'll see a document in which the authorisation of the command of the Military District in Gospic is requested. It's forward to the Ministry of Defence, to the military police administration, to Brigadier Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: 65 ter 1414. We don't have it on the screen yet. No. There are obviously some mistake in the reference. Okay, we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question is as follows: Are you aware of the fact that members of the military police started combing the terrain at a time that this area had been abandoned by members of the special police units?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which area?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Gracac, Knin, the areas affected by the operations.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I heard that the military police conducted such activities. But I was -- as I was responsible for our own operations, I didn't observe that myself. I did hear that they had certain tasks and responsibilities as a result of which they did perform such duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could we see 3D00-1441 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will see a document. It is an interim report from Colonel Rokatic [phoen], from the HQ of the Gospic Military District. It is forwarded to the headquarters, the Ministry of Defence, the police administration. It says that on the 12th of August, in the area of deployment of the HV brigade, in the course of conducting operations, an HV member was wounded, et cetera. It says that there were wounded -- or that he was wounded as a result of sniper fire. It says that the 154th HV brigade will taken responsibility for this zone, and there was a clash. Do you agree that at the time, in mid-August, there were still members of the enemy forces who had taken shelter in the forest? Do you have any knowledge about this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes absolutely. There was scores of reports that indicated that Serbian soldiers who had fled were launching attacks. At the time, an officer from our intelligence department was seriously wounded in the vicinity of Gracac. This was a time at which equipment was taken from a captured depot. There was an attack of Serbian soldiers, and this was about ten days after the Storm operation that a unit of ours was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Here, it says that, with regard to other groups, that they have 120-millimetre and 82-millimetre mortars, and they also have two tanks at their disposal; therefore, Croatian soldiers were told to be extremely cautious.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D558, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D558 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 1135. It's a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, we'll see an order from the Main Staff of the Croatian army, dated the 14th of August, 1995, in which the following is ordered. In item 1B, it says that one should start breaking up remaining enemy forces and one should commence with clearing the terrain. This order has been forwarded to the commands of the Military Districts in Bjelovar, Zagreb, Karlovac, Gospic, and Split. So, it was forwarded to Croatian army units. It says that one should act in a planned and organised when searching the terrain and when mopping-up the terrain because of straggling forces and infiltrated enemy groups. And under C, it says that one should assess the security of roads and communications, and one should assign forces to protect such routes. On the following page of the order, under D, it is said that one should expedite the sanitation of liberated areas and deal with livestock problems and other problems in cooperation with the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Ministry of Agricultural. Naturally, one should also bear in mind security-related issues. Mr. Janic, this shows that, in accordance with Main Staff order, HV units were combing the terrain, and they were involved in sanitation as well. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D559, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Mikulicic, if you would not mind - perhaps you do, but - going back to page 69, line 11 and 12, the 15 Croatian soldiers entered what place? It was my recollection that you said Donji Lapac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, this is a village which is called Uzlapac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Uzlapac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the name of the village. I'm not familiar with this region in particular, so I just read what I see in the UNMO report. So we could spell it for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It will be right in the end. I'm just a bit puzzled by what --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... similar like Donji Lapac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, no. That is not my problem. My problem is it suggests, more or less, that these 15 Croatian army soldiers, but if that was not what you wanted to establish, were, more or less, targeted where they were by the 8.35 artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I will start reading this paragraph from the very beginning, as they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... but if that -- if that is the village you had, because the grid references for the village you mentioned are quite different from the grid references for Donji Lapac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Of course. Yes. Yes, certainly. I'm aware --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm just trying to follow what your line of -- what you tried to establish in your line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I was trying to establish that HV troops are moving towards the B and H border; and afterwards, there was artillery shelled from Donji Lapac, and that is one paragraph below.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that. Of course, I was looking at the grid references as to what extent the apparent target of the artillery --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... of no importance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is of no importance at all. Oh, then, I'm relieved. Thank you very much. Then it still remains a puzzle for me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Could we see 65 ter document 654, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We'll now see a request issued to General Markac by Ante Gotovina in the Military District of Split, and he is requesting that from the forces of the special police, a battalion should be earmarked, and they should report Brigadier Ademi to be engaged in mopping-up. We've already discussed the chain of command, and we agreed that Mr. Markac's chain of command went in the direction of the Main Staff. In the right-hand corner, we can see something that is handwritten, and it says this is out of the question because under the Main Staff of the Croatian army can make such a request, such a demand. Do you have any recollection of this? Is this in accordance with the hierarchy in the structure in the field at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. Only the chief of the Main Staff of the Croatian army could issue such an order to us. That was the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, someone wonders whether you object.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry Mr. President. I do not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D560, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D560 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 1123 on the screen, please, a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We'll see an order from the Main Staff, from General Cervenko. In this order, a request is made to organise and plan the searching and mopping-up of the terrain, and special MUP units are supposed to do this and, if necessary, Croatian army units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... didn't realise that you didn't hear the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this order, special police units are ordered, yet again, to start mopping up, and this on the 21st of August. Do you have any recollection of this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 01223 becomes Exhibit number D561.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D561 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After this order was issued, special police units started carrying out task of searching the terrain which was an ongoing task. Could can we see 01226 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is a report that the order was completed, submitted by General Markac for the day 21st August 1995. Mr. Janic, are you aware that this type of report was sent on a daily basis to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those reports and the one that I see before me were sent from the Gracac headquarters, to the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And just as a reminder, they were compiled by Mr. Vranjkovic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D562.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D562 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have the report like this, dated 21st of August, in a row until 28th of August. I don't know -- 29th, sorry. I don't believe that it is necessary to go through all of these documents. In fact, my colleague has reminded me that the documents goes up to 3rd of September. I don't believe that it is necessary to go through all of them, and I will tender them from -- across the bar table, okay? Is it okay with you, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is okay with me, and, Mr. President, there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will save some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I take you that will provide Mr. Registrar with the -- how many do you means are there? If you make --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will do the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. We can do as it is. If you would have said it is fine, then Mr. Registrar could have reserved the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I could refer on ter numbers that will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you provide them to Mr. Registrar. We'll deal with them at a later stage. We know already that there is it no objection. They will be admitted, but the administration will first be completed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Just a general question with regard to these reports. In this period - meaning from 21 August up until 3 September - when mopping operations were carried out, is it your recollection that a number of enemy army members were found who were hiding in the woods and mountains, that a certain quantity of ammunitions and ordnance were found.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. Just as you mentioned it here, a number of persons were handed over to the police, and a lot of equipment was found, including depots and weapons that were left behind, vehicles, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I will just refer you to an Exhibit, a Prosecution Exhibit, P577, which is a joint report from a number of members of the special police who participated in this operation, the search and mop-up operation. And it states the number of civilians found in the field, the number of pieces of equipment found, and so on. I just want to remind you that this was quite a large number, and I won't go into it any further because this has already been admitted into evidence. Mr. Janic, I would just a few more questions that have to do with the freedom train that you mentioned yesterday. This was a train that left Zagreb and rode down the railway line from Zagreb to Split, to connect Zagreb with the previously occupied territory. And on this train was the president of Croatia, Mr. Tudjman, and a number of diplomatic representatives from Zagreb. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The anti-terrorist unit called Lucko had a special assignment because it was supposed to secure the railway tracks at the most sensitive spot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please move into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It's a document dated September 1st, in which the commander of the Gospic Military District reports to the Main Staff and the operations administration, stating that the units during the search operations were engaged by the enemy. They had fire contact, and it is assessed that there still some groups in the wider area of the Plitvice waterfalls remaining. Is this consistent with what you recalled, that there were straggling enemy groups in the area, in the woods and hills, at this time?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know who is waiting and for what reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am waiting for the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did I miss something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I see is that the last word is the answer of the witness and then it stops. So I didn't know that you were waiting to hear from Ms. Mahindaratne whether she would object.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't realise that a document had been tendered into evidence. If it is the document on the screen, I don't have any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is the 1st of September document. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D564, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D564 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janic, after the special police completed their mission in the area of Gracac, the area surrounding Knin and so on, a new mission was set forth in the area of Plitvice. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see document 01707.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: This is a report submitted by Mr. Markac to the chief of the Main Staff, on the completed mission, on the 6th of September, in Plitvice. Mention is made here of what kind of area had been searched and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a number of documents identical to this one, relating to the particular day when the operation was carried out; and if there is no opposition, I would like to tender these documents across the bar table. [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... reach final point. Could I have three or four minutes more, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D565.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D565 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When this operation was completed, document 01831 was issued, which is a joint report on the mopping-up operation of the general area ever of the Plitvice national park, conducted by special police units. And this document mentions the number of ordnance found, 02831. So this document mentions the ammunition found, the de-mining of certain parts of the national park, the Plitvice national park; in other words, about providing security in the area. Mr. Janic, can you confirm that the special police participated in this operation which was called Operation Oluja-Plitvice.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D566, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D566 is ... [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see document 1778.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We were too quick for the transcription -- D566 is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- admitted into evidence. If you would please wait until the transcript stops moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see here that this is a document, an analysis of the employment of the military police in Operation Storm, in which, on page 3 of the document, there is an description of -- or a report that the mopping-up of towns and settled areas was carried out immediately after the members of the Croatian army moved through the area, and by, AT, anti-terrorists units of the police. "AT" stands for anti-terrorist. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So we can see here in this document what the role of the special police was in the clearing up of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I would like appreciate a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D567, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D567 is admitted into evidence. Just looking on what I see on my screen, what paragraph were you referring to exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm referring on paragraph 3.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 3.2, yes. That is it not on my screen. That may explain --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... page three of the whole document on the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll find my way. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janic, my last question. For many years, you worked with Mr. Markac. Could you please tell us, in a few words, what kind of cooperation you had, and what your impressions of Mr. Markac as a commander of the special police was?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've known Mr. Markac for over 20 years now. We worked together for many years, we were the closest associates, and, as a friend and colleague, I can say that is he a modest, responsible, and honourable man and police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers, Mr. Janic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That concludes my cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. Matters are still the same as far as Gotovina and Cermak Defence are concerned. Then, Ms. Mahindaratne, you asked 15 minutes, if you could try to complete your re-examination well within that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, may I call documents 65 ter 1417, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, now, yesterday, you were cross-examined about the special police units which were attached to the police administrations and about the relationship between the chief of the police administrations and those units. Now, are you familiar with this document which is on your screen at the moment?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's an official publication of the Croatian Ministry of Interior, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this has both the B/C/S and the English translation within the document itself. If we could move to page 8, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, I don't want to waste time, but this page explains about how the police administrations were organised, and lists out what the police administrations were.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And we could move on to page 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janic, those were the different sections of the Ministry of Interior, isn't it, and special police is at number 3? I mean the document reflects it, then I will move on.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could move to page 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There is this paragraph, the Ministry of Interior is organised on the following levels. Number one refers to central administration, and number 2 is police administration; then it says 20 police administrations which follow the county system of the Republic of Croatia and the reception centre, and it goes on. Now this police administrations were a geographical organisation, and the Ministry of Interior was divided into the police administration for administrative purposes, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the state of Croatia is divided into 20 counties, 20 regions, in administrative terms; and each county, or rather, each region had its own police administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could move on to page 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That actually gives the full chart, part of which Mr. Mikulicic tendered yesterday without the top part. That's a correct chart, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, any objection against --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No objection, just a request for clarification. The document that was just shown on the screen, is it original from 1995 or what is time of the issuance of this document? Could you give us a reference, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, the chart that you tendered yesterday is identical -- the bottom half is identical. What is missing in the chart that you tendered is the top half, top part. So it's your chart related to this -- that time-frame is the same time-frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document certainly does not date back to 1995 since in one of the annexes it gives informs what happened in 1996, so that couldn't be the case. Ms. Mahindaratne, is, however, entitled to ask a question. Of course, she could also ask whether that part of the hierarchical structure had changed since 1995. But at least she is entitled to ask whether what she - and I couldn't verify that yet - what she considered to be the same bottom part, whether it would be complete if the top part as shown on the screen would be added to it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry to interrupt. I think it would be only be fair to find out the dates within which each of those charts are -- are constructed for the witness to be able to answer, I think, fairly accurately.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'll ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, even if you would not know the date, sometimes if you are acquainted with the content, then the date might not be of importance. I take it, Ms. Mahindaratne, that you have carefully checked that the bottom part is in every respect the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may ask questions on contents and then when this was created, made; and after that, it may be an issue, but not at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, perhaps could you tell us if this chart reflects the organisational framework of the Ministry of Interior. Now was this accurate even for 1995? Is this how it was organised? And I appreciate you would not being able to speak about the other sectors, but with regard to the special police sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Could we have a translation on the screen for the witness, please, because --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes. The next page is in B/C/S, the chart, if we could -- or maybe the previous page. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's accurate. But may I just point something out with your permission. The entire document, or, rather, this book, as far as I can remember, this book isn't an official document from the Ministry of Internal Affairs. It a book that printed both in English and in Croatian and it was given to foreign delegations that would come to visit the Ministry of Internal Affairs. It was to provide them with information about our system. So it was a book that had been published in order to distribute it to foreign delegations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, that's perhaps the reason why Ms. Mahindaratne seeks verification of the accuracy of the booklet. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could move on to page 29.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And we are -- if we look at the third paragraph and I will just quickly read the relevant part. The reference to special police and it says: "The special police, according to the inner structure, consists of the special police sector with its departments," and it lists all the departments, "in according with the territorial organisation of the --" I'm sorry, I missed a part. "... and other units which are located in police administrations in accordance with the territorial organisation of the Republic of Croatia." Now, it says that the units which are located -- are located in police administration.
