Now, as I understand, Mr. Janic, it says that the special police units are located in police administrations and I don't read it as a -- as if these units come within the command structure of the police administrations. Can you be -- you would be in a very good position to explain to the Trial Chamber what exactly the scenario is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Scenario of what?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What exactly the relationship was between the special police units which were attached to the police administrations and the police administration. Was it an administrative arrangement?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain how this functioned. Well, for example police administration had five police stations and a special unit. So the special unit of a police administration had the same administrative relationship with the head of the police administration, as was the case for some police stations within that police administration. So the hierarchy was strictly established. You had the chief of the police administration at the head, then you had the deputy chief, then you had departments. You had the police departments, you had the crime police department, you had the traffic police department. And then at the level of departments you had the special units.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now we saw yesterday a number of reports submitted by the special police units after their operations to the special police sector. Now did the unit commanders of the special police units attached to the police administrations submit reports on their daily activity, the mop-up operations, for instance, to the chiefs of the police administrations? And we saw the reports sent to the special police sector. Now my question is: Did they submit such reports to the special -- the police administration chiefs?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't submit such daily reports but upon returning to their base they would send reports to the chief of the administration on what they had done during the course of their engagement. But they didn't submit such daily reports, not with the sector of police units although they were under the command of the sector of special police units at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And did the chiefs of the police administrations take decisions about the operations or the activity of the special police units attached to the administrations? And decisions, when I say, as to what operations they should carry out. Or was it all controlled by special police sector?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the police administration planned and led units in all situations in which the unit carried out its duties in the territory of the police administration. When the unit was called to join forces --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my question was whether the chiefs of the police administrations, and I'm not referring to the unit commanders of the special police unit but the chief of the police administrations, did he decide on the activities that the special police units should carry out and issue orders such as, you know, for example, carry out a mop-up operation in such-and-such an area. The kind of orders that we saw yesterday being issued by Mr. Markac and Mr. Sacic?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They issued ordered for certain tasks not for searching the terrain, because the units, when it came to those tasks, were under the command of the sector. But they did issue tasks or, rather, orders for other tasks. For example, if there was a certain situation in Osijek, it was the special sector in Osijek that had to receive an order from the chief in Osijek, from the police sector in Osijek, for example, if there was a kidnapping case, a hostage case.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Due to lack of time I will quickly move on, Mr. Janic, since I have to cover another area. Just one last question on that. Now, if disciplinary measures had to be meted out against members of the Lucko unit within whose area of responsibility did that fall? I mean since the Lucko unit stood independently would that be the special police sector?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that went beyond what the scope of the cross was and there was nothing discussed there in cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There was a reference to the Lucko unit not being attached to the police administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have seen at least the statistics on disciplinary matters. Now, to be quite honest, I don't know whether that was in chief or on cross. You see it is not all the same to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In cross, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In cross. Then please answer the question, Witness, Mr. Janic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the question please be repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who was competent for imposing disciplinary measures in the Lucko unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander of the unit was responsible for disciplinary measures, in relation to unit members. So the commander had this responsibility and authority. It was part of his job description to initiate or to take disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janic, you are the -- you are currently the commander of the special police, if you see one of your subordinate units are suspected of committing a crime and you don't see any investigations initiated against that, what would you do?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify the question. It is not quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: As commander of the special police your informed that your subordinate units may have -- are suspected of committing a crime and you see or it is brought to your notice that the unit commander responsible for taking or initiating investigation or meting out disciplinary measures has failed to do so, what would you do, as commander of the special police?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would then write to him and inform him of the facts I am aware of and I would warn him about his duty to initiate disciplinary procedures.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Going to another area due to lack of time. Now, Mr. Janic, you testified about artillery support that you asked for during the course of the attack. Now, you said that there were pre-determined targets. Were there any pre-determined targets in civilian populated areas in your line of attack?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't. Which stage are we talking about, the first stage of Operation Storm or the entire operation --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Operation Storm, the first stage on 4th and 5th August?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My line of attack was Velebit, Celavac, up until Prezid, so up until the road. This was an uninhabited area; there weren't even villages in that area in my line of attack. Apart from the first and second enemy lines and up to the Celavac repeater, there were no other facilities. There were no other buildings so there weren't any targets --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- targets that you are referring to now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What were the pre-determined targets? Were they soldiers or were there any other military installations or equipment, what were the pre-determined targets?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pre-determined targets were the enemy positions and the depth of their defence line the artillery positions their command post, their depots, the targets were the enemy infrastructure that they used to defend their lines. Those were the exclusive targets that we had. Whenever conducting an operation, well, it wasn't possible to have any other targets. All the targets were military targets. The purpose was to breakthrough the enemy defence line and to attain the operation's objectives. It wasn't possible to have any other objectives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, I asked to you finish within the 15 minutes. You've taken substantially more.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just have two minutes please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Perhaps I would have a question as well. I limited you and to -- also I'm also looking at how you use your time, and I can imagine that you would have started with the last subject rather than the other ones, prioritising matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A report was put to you, 21st of August, reporting on the activities and it was said that there were similar reports for every day. Now that report of the 24th [sic] of August mentions that at noon, Mr. Gotovina, Mr. Cermak, and Mr. Markac met briefly. Do you know anything about that meeting, on the 21st of August?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you -- have you any idea about the frequency of the gentlemen I just mentioned meeting in this period of time, in Knin? So the three of them together.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have any knowledge of that. They were high-level officials and I couldn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was my question. Have the questions in cross or the questions by the Bench triggered any need for further questions, Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Janic, this concludes your evidence. I'm happy that at least where you had a strong wish to return today that at least we could meet that wish. I've one question for you. Earlier we discussed the possibility that the original of the handwritten report you said you may have at home, to be given to this Tribunal for inspection, not to lose it forever but for inspection. Would you please check at home whether you can find it; and then the Victims and Witness Section will give you the -- the details of our Zagreb office, and you're invited, if you find it, to hand it over to them. I then take it that you'll get a receipt for giving it. And if we would receive it, of course, it will be shared with the parties for inspection. Mr. Janic, I would like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague, for answered all the questions by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again. And of course, first of all, a timely trip home again. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, we will adjourn until Monday, quarter past 2.00. That is Monday, the 14th of July, quarter past 2.00 in courtroom number II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of July, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
